//: ECS Fargate task definition for the scheduler. Same image as the API, different switches. Run this service with desiredCount 1 and a deployment configuration of maximumPercent 100 / minimumHealthyPercent 0, so ECS stops the old task before starting the new one and two schedulers never overlap.
//why-separate: Quartz here uses UseInMemoryStore, so every process that has the scheduler enabled runs every job. Two API tasks with Scheduler:Enabled=true would dispatch every campaign twice, send every expiry reminder twice and drain the email outbox twice. Splitting the schedule into its own single-task service is the smallest change that makes the API horizontally scalable; the alternative is Quartz clustering with an AdoJobStore, which needs its own tables and a migration.

containerDefinitions.name: worker
containerDefinitions.//portMappings: None. This task is not behind the load balancer; it listens on 8080 only so its own health check has something to answer.
containerDefinitions.//stopTimeout: Longer than the API's. WaitForJobsToComplete lets a campaign dispatch finish rather than being cut in half mid-batch.

environment.//: The one process on the platform with this set to true.
environment.name: Scheduler__Enabled

environment.//: The export consumer runs here too. That is deliberate and safe: MassTransit consumers are competing consumers, so the API tasks and this one share the queue rather than duplicating it. Scheduled jobs are the only thing that must be singular.
environment.name: RabbitMQ__Enabled
